t: A 6,000 kg GVW goods vehicle aged 1 year 10 months carries IMT 23. In an accident the vehicle body (metal, Rs 30,000) and two tyres (Rs 16,000) are damaged; labour Rs 5,000. The claim payable is
e: Tyres: 50% depreciation gives Rs 8,000, then the insured bears 50% under IMT 23, leaving Rs 4,000. Metal 10% (1-2 years) = Rs 27,000. Labour Rs 5,000. Total Rs 36,000 less compulsory deductible Rs 500 (GVW not exceeding 7,500 kg) = Rs 35,500.

t: Section 56 provides that a transport vehicle whose fitness certificate has expired shall
o: Continue to be validly registered for 30 days
Be treated as a non-transport vehicle
Not be deemed validly registered under Section 39
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Without a valid certificate of fitness a transport vehicle is not deemed to be validly registered, which has direct bearing on claim admissibility.

t: A car is insured with two different insurers; the later policy (annual premium Rs 6,000) is cancelled under GR 24 after running 73 days of 365 with no claim. The refund is
e: In double insurance with different insurers the later policy is cancelled with pro-rata refund: Rs 6,000 x 292/365 = Rs 4,800.

t: A policy (annual premium Rs 6,000) is extended by 2 months under GR 11 to align the renewal date, pro-rata premium being charged. The insured then does not renew with the same insurer. He must additionally pay
o: Rs 800, the difference between short period premium (30%) and pro-rata premium
e: GR 11: extension for less than 12 months is allowed on pro-rata premium (2/12 x 6,000 = Rs 1,000) provided the policy is renewed with the same insurer; otherwise the insured pays the difference between short period (30% = Rs 1,800) and pro-rata rates = Rs 800.

t: A two wheeler package policy is extended under IMT 31 for a rally. During the rally the deductible under Section I is
o: Rs 2,500 or the IMT 22 deductible, whichever is higher
nil, as the rally premium replaces the deductible
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). IMT 31 inserts Rs 5,000 for private cars and Rs 2,500 for two wheelers; for the duration of the event the Section I deductible is this amount or the IMT 22 amount, whichever is higher. Organised racing, pace making and speed testing remain excluded.

t: An insured cancels his private car policy (annual premium Rs 9,000, no claim) exactly 5 months after inception. The refund under GR 24 is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Cancellation by the insured attracts short period retention: exceeding 4 months but not exceeding 5 months = 60% retained (Rs 5,400); refund = Rs 9,000 - Rs 5,400 = Rs 3,600.

t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations 2024, the free-look period for a policy with a term of one year or more is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 30 days from receipt of the policy document, irrespective of the sales channel.

t: Under a Class E road transit policy for brand new chassis with new tyres, the 50% limitation on tyres can be deleted on payment of
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Deletion of the 50% limitation clause for tyres and tubes under Class E is permitted only for brand new vehicles with brand new tyres on payment of 1% of basic OD premium using IMT 62.

t: Nomination and assignment of a life insurance policy are governed respectively by which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 39 deals with nomination; Section 38 with assignment and transfer.

t: Under Section 19, on a first offence referred by the licensing authority, the driver may be disqualified from holding a licence for
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). First offence attracts disqualification of 3 months; a second or subsequent offence leads to revocation, and a refresher course is required before return of the licence.

t: Under Section 130, a driver must on demand produce documents for examination to
e: Section 130 obliges the driver/conductor to produce licence, insurance, fitness and permit on demand by a police officer in uniform.

t: Under IRDAI's 2024 norms, a surveyor must be appointed within what time of a claim intimation?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Appointment within 24 hours; survey report within 15 days; insurer's decision within 7 days of the report.

t: A car's IDV is ₹5,00,000 and the wreck fetches ₹80,000 on an 'as is where is' basis. The maximum insurer liability on a total loss basis where the insured retains the wreck is
e: Insurer's liability cannot exceed IDV less the value of the wreck, i.e. ₹4,20,000 before policy deductibles.

t: Under GR 36B the premium for optional PA cover to named persons in a private car (IMT 15) is, per Rs 10,000 of CSI,
e: GR 36B rates per Rs 10,000 CSI or part thereof: private car Rs 5, motorised two wheeler Rs 7, commercial vehicle Rs 6.

t: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance, after the 2024 IRDAI changes, is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Reduced from 48 to 36 months; the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) is 60 months.

t: A particular surveyor repeatedly fails to submit reports within 7 days. The office should
o: deduct 10% from his fee for each delayed report
bring the recurrence of delay to the notice of the Regional Office
e: If the surveyor delays he must give a status report with reasons; in case of recurrence of delay by a particular surveyor it should be brought to the Regional Office's notice.

t: Section 164 (earlier 163A) compensation for grievous hurt without proof of fault is
e: Section 164 provides ₹5 lakh for death and ₹2.5 lakh for grievous hurt; the claimant need not establish negligence.

t: A new car with a listed selling price of Rs 12,00,000 is 5 months old at the time of insurance. Its IDV under GR 8 is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR 8 schedule: not exceeding 6 months - 5% depreciation; Rs 12,00,000 x 95% = Rs 11,40,000.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to start a life or general insurance company in India is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹100 crore for a direct insurer; ₹200 crore for a reinsurer (Section 6 of the Insurance Act).

t: Under IMT-23, items excluded by IMT-21 can be covered on payment of extra premium, with the claim payable at
e: IMT-23 buys back the IMT-21 exclusion for commercial vehicles on extra premium, but only 50% of the loss is payable.

t: The own damage premium of a car before NCB is Rs 18,000 and the insured has three consecutive claim-free years. The NCB amount is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR 27: NCB for three consecutive claim-free years is 35%; 35% of Rs 18,000 = Rs 6,300, leaving a net OD premium of Rs 11,700.

t: A corporate agent may tie up with a maximum of how many insurers in each line of business?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 3 to 9 insurers per category (life, general, health) by the 2022 amendment to the Corporate Agents Regulations.

t: In addition to the 25% OD discount, a certified vintage car is allowed a discount on TP premium of
o: 50%, as directed by IRDA with effect from 1.4.2018
nil - TP premium is never discounted
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR 29 gives 25% discount on OD premium to vintage cars certified by the Vintage and Classic Car Club of India; a 50% discount on TP premium was additionally allowed from 1.4.2018.

t: A fire and/or theft only policy under GR 45A (without liability cover) may be issued only when
o: the insured specifically requests in writing that the vehicle will not be used at all during the entire policy period
the vehicle is more than 10 years old
the insured has a Liability Only policy with another insurer
the vehicle is a commercial vehicle under Class D
e: GR 45A permits fire and/or theft only cover at the specific written request of the insured that during the entire policy period the vehicle will not be used at all; it is prohibited for Classes D, E, F and G.

t: A cinema publicity van insured with IMT 50 suffers damage to a detachable sound amplifier mounted on it during an accident. The loss to the amplifier is
o: covered as an accessory of the vehicle
not covered, as equipment is covered only if firmly and permanently fixed to the body and not detachable
e: IMT 50 excludes loss or damage to cinematic, photographic or sound equipment, costumes or other technical property on the vehicle unless firmly and permanently fixed to the body and not detachable from time to time.

t: As per the trainer's summary of the 2024 master circular, the insurer must decide a claim within how many days of receiving the survey report?
e: The circular requires the survey report within 15 days and the insurer's decision within 7 days thereafter, followed by immediate payment.

t: The minimum value for premium computation of a four wheeled passenger vehicle with carrying capacity of 12 passengers is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Four wheeled passenger vehicles carrying more than 6 but not more than 17 passengers have a minimum IDV of Rs 20,000; the corresponding three wheelers have Rs 25,000; 17-36 passengers Rs 30,000.

t: Under Section 54, registration suspended under Section 53 may be cancelled if the suspension continues uninterrupted for not less than
e: Cancellation follows when suspension for being unroadworthy or dangerous continues for at least six months.

t: A private car package policy is extended under IMT 31 for a rally lasting 4 days. The additional premium is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Rally extension for private car package policies: Rs 60 for the first day and Rs 30 for each succeeding day: 60 + 3 x 30 = Rs 150 (liability only policies: Rs 25 and Rs 15).

t: A car with IDV Rs 6,00,000 is kept in a garage and not used. The insured requests cover for fire and theft only under GR 45A. The premium is
e: GR 45A rates: fire only 0.50% of IDV, theft only 0.50%, fire and theft 0.75%; Rs 6,00,000 x 0.75% = Rs 4,500 (IMT 26 attached).
